nation: Early Woodland caves and rockshelters (archaeological period)
presenceNote: This story is about a site, not a mapped area: nothing is drawn. Early Woodland is an archaeological period (about 1000 to 200 BC), not a named culture. The Kentucky Archaeological Survey notes that rockshelter use and cave mining peaked then. Newt Kash Hollow, Cloudsplitter Rockshelter and Salts Cave are known sites, and no source used here gives an area for them, so only each story's pin is shown. Archaeological sites defined by artifacts and dates, not a tribe; no descent claim is made.
overlapNote: No area is drawn, so there is nothing to overlap.
basis: Kentucky Archaeological Survey, Woodland-period chapter (public agency source).
